jobs.prompt: The owner approved docs/architecture/swarm-v2.md with three changes; apply them to that file and to docs/scope/roadmap.md. CHANGES. (1) Stage 1 adds per-job TEST DATABASE and PORT isolation, without containers: each job that runs tests or an e2e suite gets its own test database (own name or own file) and its own ports allocated by swarm, nothing shared between concurrent jobs; exit gate: the e2e suite passes 5 times in parallel on one Mac with zero shared data (no two runs touch the same database, port, temp folder or file). (2) Stage 1 adds enforced permissions the cheap way: a branch-only push token (a fine-grained GitHub personal access token limited to the selected active repositories, with Contents read and write, Pull requests read and write, Metadata read, Actions read, and NO Administration, NO Workflows write, NO Secrets or Environments permission, so it can push feature branches and open pull requests but not change settings or workflows) plus branch protection on main in every active repository (pull request required, no force pushes, no deletions, enforced for admins, required checks as set today); the owner is shown the exact token scopes before it is created and creates it in the GitHub settings page; exit gate: an orchestrator session using that token can push a feature branch and open a PR, and a push to main (also a force push and a delete) is rejected by the server. (3) Order after stage 1: chief orchestrator, then per-job container isolation with enforced permissions at the service, then the multi-machine cluster, then cloud burst. Keep the flags-off-by-default rollout for every part. EDIT docs/architecture/swarm-v2.md: keep the existing structure and facts; split item 4 into 4a (stage 1: test database and port isolation plus the cheap enforced permissions: today, gap, effort M, migration) and 4b (later: containers and service-enforced permissions: effort L); add a section Stage 1 (internal, about one month) right before Suggested order that lists the stage 1 scope with weeks: weeks 1 to 2 event store (events table, views, importers, dual publish; gate: the board answers from the store with the same numbers as today's files on project-swarm); weeks 2 to 3 state outside the repo (pointer file, swarm migrate state, dual write; gate: git status clean after a full wave); weeks 3 to 4 swarm add and a stronger doctor plus a minimal opt-in service under launchd that owns the store and the machine limit (gate: restart and clients reconnect within 5 seconds; swarm add shows a project on the board in under 60 seconds); weeks 2 to 4 in parallel test database and port isolation (gate above) and the branch-only token with branch protection (gate above); and state what stage 1 does not include. Rewrite Suggested order to: stage 1 as above (event store first, then state outside the repo, then test DB and ports isolation and the branch-only token in parallel, then swarm add and doctor, then the service MVP), then chief orchestrator, then container isolation (4b), then cluster, then cloud burst; and note the Node constraint: the event store uses the built-in node:sqlite module, which exists from Node 22.13 and not in Node 20, so on Node 20 the store feature is off and its tests are skipped with a stated reason, and dropping Node 20 support (raising the engines floor) is a decision for the owner. Keep the document within 140 lines and in plain short sentences. EDIT docs/scope/roadmap.md: replace the current section S7 and its requirements R-040 to R-047 with two stages, keeping all text outside them unchanged: update the Stages list to S7 Swarm v2 stage 1 (internal, about one month) and S8 Swarm v2 later stages; section ## S7 Swarm v2 stage 1 with R-040 The event store answers the board (one events table in SQLite, importers from the existing ndjson and markdown files, dual publish, a feature flag off by default, parity with today's numbers; skipped with a reason on Node 20), R-041 Swarm state lives outside the repo (state folder per project under the machine data folder, a committed pointer, swarm migrate state with dual write, git status clean after a full wave), R-042 swarm add registers a project in one command (swarm add REPO, stronger swarm doctor checks, the project shown on the board in under 60 seconds), R-043 A per-machine swarm service runs under launchd (opt in, owns the event store and the machine limit, CLI keeps working when it is off, clients reconnect within 5 seconds after a restart), R-044 Concurrent jobs share no test data (per-job test database and ports, the e2e suite passes 5 times in parallel on one Mac with zero shared data), R-045 Pushes are limited by the server (branch-only fine-grained push token with the exact scopes listed, branch protection on every active repository, a push to main rejected). Then ## S8 Swarm v2 later stages with R-046 One chief orchestrator plans across projects, R-047 Jobs run in containers with permissions enforced by the service, R-048 One queue and one board across machines, R-049 Cloud runners take overflow work, each with 2 or 3 measurable acceptance lines in the file's existing format (a heading line, a one-sentence outcome title, Acceptance: then bullet lines with numbers or commands, no vague words like clean or robust). The roadmap must then have 49 requirements and 8 stages. Write only docs/architecture/swarm-v2.md and docs/scope/roadmap.md.
